label: live

steps.assertion: The Pro project terminal opens in its registered dedicated checkout.
The dev-madrid device terminal uses the existing relay and prints the actual remote hostname.
Type or dictate a command and Run send echo hello through the real PTY.
Sticky Ctrl and C interrupt sleep within two seconds and preserve its non-zero exit record.
Reload reconnects the same terminal and replays hello in its scrollback.
The copy buttons include exactly the requested command range and strip every escape code.

steps.assertion: Send to… delivers the last command to the coordinator and starts its next turn.

evidence.text:

record-6

steps.assertion: Take over in browser attaches a real native thread session; leaving detaches and returns it to Jevellan.
Every captured screen passes the dedicated live vision rubric in this layout.

screens.expected: a connected project terminal with usable controls and no clipped text

cosmetic: The last key in the control row (after →) is cut off at the right edge. It looks like the row scrolls sideways, but nothing on screen shows there are more keys.
The header path is shortened with an ellipsis ('/Users/ggomes...'), so the full project path isn't visible.
Terminal output breaks words partway through ('jevellan-l / ive-sandbox', 'jevellan-live- / sandbox') because the terminal is narrow.
There's a lot of empty space below the output and a stray horizontal line near the bottom of the terminal area.

screens.expected: a connected dev-madrid terminal with the remote hostname and usable controls

cosmetic: The row of key buttons runs past the right edge. A partly visible button after '→' suggests the row scrolls sideways, but nothing shows that it scrolls.
A stray 'hostname' line appears at the top of the terminal, above the first prompt, which looks like the command was echoed twice.
The terminal has a lot of empty space below the output, and the black cursor or underline bar sits at the very bottom, away from the prompt.

screens.expected: terminal copy and Send to controls reachable at this layout

cosmetic: The header path is cut off at the right edge ('/Users/ggomes…'), so the full working directory isn't visible.

The quick-key row runs to the edge of the screen: the '…' button on the right is tight against or slightly past the edge, and the '→' button on the left is close to the edge too. The row may need horizontal scrolling.
Long shell prompts wrap in the middle of words in the terminal output ('jevellan-live-' / 'sandbox %'), which makes them a little harder to read.
The 'Copied' confirmation is a plain text label sitting away from the button that was tapped, so it's easy to miss.

screens.expected: a browser terminal attached to a resumed native coding session, past setup and trust dialogs, with usable exit controls

cosmetic: The status line at the bottom of the terminal is cut off at the right edge: 'bypass permissions on (shift+tab to' is missing its ending.
The on-screen key row (Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, arrows) runs past the right edge. The last key is only partly visible and must be scrolled into view.
The terminal text wraps tightly at this narrow width. For example, the node path in the stop-hook error is split across lines, which makes it a little harder to read.
The terminal output shows a stop hook error (/bin/sh: node: not found). This is a problem in the session's setup, not a layout problem, but it stands out on screen.

observations: Usage records come from runtime-reported turn outcomes. Missing tokens or cost remain unknown; minutes include concurrent sessions.
